repo_notes.content: Rigor is a type-aware static bug finder for Ruby that requires zero annotations and imposes zero runtime dependencies. It parses code using Prism and infers types directly from the values produced by expressions. Key architectural commitments: (1) Types are facts, not wishes: types are derived from actual execution semantics rather than aspirational comments; (2) False positives outrank worst-case static reading: findings fire only when the receiver type is conclusively known and evidence is sound (tested against corpora like Mastodon, Redmine, GitLab FOSS); (3) Programmable inference beyond unions: tracks literal values, integer ranges, refinements (e.g., non-empty-string), tuple and hash shapes, and effect labels.
repo_notes.author: Rigor Maintainers

repo_notes.content: Domain glossary and terminology traps (defined in CONTEXT.md): (1) 'interface' ALWAYS means structural typing (like Go interfaces or Python Protocols; satisfied by methods, no 'implements' clause); never Java/PHP nominal interfaces. (2) 'protocol' is strictly reserved for ADR-28 path-scoped behavioral method contracts in plugin manifests. (3) 'scope' is overloaded: Rigor::Scope is the immutable inference state; 'analysis scope' is the set of files analyzed in a run; 'publish set' is the LSP notification target. (4) 'Dynamic[T]' is gradual typing ('statically unknown, believed within envelope T') and carries a dynamic origin explaining why it is dynamic (ADR-75, ADR-82). (5) 'erasure' is the conservative mapping of rich internal carriers back to standard RBS.
repo_notes.author: Rigor Maintainers

repo_notes.content: Repository layout and documentation authority: (1) Normative specifications: docs/type-specification/ (type system) and docs/internal-spec/ (inference engine contracts) are binding. (2) Architecture Decision Records: docs/adr/ explains the rationale behind architectural decisions; docs/adr/README.md is the complete index. (3) Core implementation lives in lib/rigor/ (engine, CLI, language server, MCP server, cache, effects). (4) Production framework plugins live in plugins/ (Rails, ActiveRecord, RSpec, Sorbet bridge, Sidekiq, Devise, dry-rb, and more; plugins/README.md is the inventory); examples/ holds plugin-contract walkthroughs, not production support. (5) User-facing agent skills that Rigor ships to adopting projects live in skills/ (e.g. rigor-next-steps, rigor-ask, rigor-project-init; skills/README.md is the inventory); .claude/skills/ holds contributor-only workflows for this repository and is not part of the product. Upstream submodules in references/ are read-only upstream material.
repo_notes.author: Rigor Maintainers

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: High-level introduction to Rigor: what it is, its core philosophy (inference-first, no inline annotations, zero runtime dependency), key capabilities, and how the major subsystems relate. Links to child pages for installation, configuration, contribution, and editor/agent integrations. Covers recent additions such as effect labels (ADR-103), unused-code reachability (ADR-102), checked types and typeless comments (ADR-107), type provenance for agents (ADR-108), Ruby-native range notation (ADR-109), inherited declaration precedence (ADR-110), and inline refinement carrier (ADR-111).

page_notes.content: Start with README.md, AGENTS.md, and CONTEXT.md. Emphasize that Rigor is a developer tool and static bug detector, not a type system compiler or runtime type checker.

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.purpose: Installation (mise, gem install, Nix flake, container images), quick-start workflow, running rigor check, reading diagnostic output, and core daily commands (init, annotate, type-of, triage, sig-gen, doctor, effects, unused). Explains that Rigor is a global tool running on Ruby 4.0 while analyzing application code running on any Ruby version.

page_notes.content: Reference docs/install.md, docs/manual/01-installation.md, and docs/manual/02-cli-reference.md. Highlight global mise installation (mise use -g ruby@4.0 gem:rigortype) keeping tool dependencies separated from project Gemfiles.

page_notes.content: Source code in lib/rigor/configuration/. Reference schemas/rigor-config.schema.json, docs/manual/03-configuration.md, and ADR-99.

pages.title: Contributing and Development Setup

page_notes.content: Strictly follow AGENTS.md operating rules: run development commands via 'nix develop --command <cmd>', emphasize 'make verify-changed' over full-suite runs, and reference docs/agents/contribution-flow.md.

page_notes.content: Primary normative reference is docs/type-specification/ and docs/types.md. Code in lib/rigor/type/. Foundational decisions in ADR-1 and ADR-3.

Normalization rules, trinary certainty system, Type::Combinator, dynamic-origin algebra (ADR-83), Dynamic[T] provenance (ADR-75, ADR-82, ADR-108), and Ruby-native range notation (ADR-109).

page_notes.content: Inspect lib/rigor/type/ and docs/internal-spec/internal-type-api.md for carrier contracts and certainty representation.
